issuing_body: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Minnesota / U.S. Department of Justice
title: U.S. Attorney Announces Federal Charges Against 47 Defendants in $250 Million Feeding Our Future Fraud Scheme
supports: DOJ announced federal criminal charges against 47 defendants in the initial public Feeding Our Future charging wave on 2022-09-20.

DOJ alleged a scheme involving approximately $250 million in Federal Child Nutrition Program funds and stated Feeding Our Future opened more than 250 sites and fraudulently obtained and disbursed more than $240 million.
DOJ alleged Feeding Our Future employees recruited individuals/entities to open sites, false meal counts and attendance rosters were used, and shell companies were used to receive/launder proceeds.
DOJ's charging narrative states that when MDE pressed Aimee Bock for clarification, Bock accused MDE of discrimination/unfair scrutiny and that Feeding Our Future sued over denied site applications.
does_not_support: The $250 million figure is a charging/alleged scheme figure, not a court-certified restitution or collected-loss total.
The release does not prove every allegation against every defendant; indictments are allegations until adjudicated.
The fact that Feeding Our Future litigated against MDE does not establish that a court ordered MDE to resume reimbursement payments; the Minnesota Judicial Branch separately corrected that claim.
